answer: Trust propagates through a weighted attestation graph by bounded-length random walks, limiting influence to reachable verified paths. A sybil cluster with few links to honest nodes has low conductance: its outgoing edge weight is small relative to its volume. Min-cut bounds then constrain probability mass crossing the cluster boundary, while bounded walk length limits transitive amplification. Thus labels such as nadir, yarrow, and harbor add no voting weight absent costly, durable bridges.
